picks.title: I finally tried XREAL's fully-baked Android XR glasses, and now I'm counting down to launch
picks.excerpt: Android Authority went hands-on with XREAL's Aura, the first fully-realized Android XR glasses, arguing the Gemini-driven eyewear points to an Android you use without pulling out a phone screen.
picks.rationale: First hands-on with a finished Android XR device — the clearest signal yet of what a screenless, Gemini-first interface actually looks like for designers.

picks.title: Anthropic's Claude Comes to CarPlay
picks.excerpt: Anthropic added CarPlay support to the Claude iOS app, so drivers can talk to Claude through in-car infotainment now that iOS 26.4 opens CarPlay to third-party chatbots.
picks.rationale: A shipped feature, not a roadmap: iOS 26.4 opening CarPlay to third-party assistants makes the car a real surface designers now have to lay out for.

picks.title: DJI's second-gen Romo robot vacuum looks like the lovechild of an HR Giger drawing and an iMac G3
picks.excerpt: DJI's second-gen Romo robot vacuum borrows drone navigation know-how for precise mapping, and adds hardware privacy measures after the first generation's hacking embarrassment.
picks.rationale: Rare case of a hack forcing privacy into the industrial design itself — drone-grade perception plus physical safeguards as a visible product decision.

picks.title: Withings' 'Thermometer of the Future' Is Getting an AI Analysis Upgrade
picks.excerpt: Withings' BeamO multi-scope device gains an AI analysis layer that interprets its own heart and lung recordings, pushing consumer health hardware toward on-device interpretation.
picks.rationale: Consumer health hardware moves from capturing signals to interpreting them — a hard design problem in how much a device is allowed to tell you.

picks.title: Stripped-down Windows 11 for AI developers demands 64GB RAM and insane 250 GB/s bandwidth — Project Zenith will debut on AMD's flagship Ryzen AI Halo platform
picks.excerpt: Microsoft's stripped-down Windows 11 'Project Zenith' for AI developers demands 64GB of RAM and 250 GB/s of bandwidth, debuting on AMD's Ryzen AI Halo platform.
picks.rationale: Microsoft carving out an OS SKU just for local-AI work sets a concrete hardware floor for anyone planning to run models on their own machine.

Already covered inside published 'gadgets-nvidia-rtx-spark-ai-pcs' (WIRED, 09-04), which reports the ThinkCentre X Ultra with Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 / 128GB / $3,699.
Same Wear OS 7 offline-Gemini rollout already published as 'gadgets-pixel-watch5-offline-gemini' (09-03).

notes: User deferred, so picks are curator-scored. Wide pool of 22 survivors; six dropped for URL/content duplication against the last 5 days of sections.gadgets (today 09-06 through 09-01). Backfilled to a full 5 with never-before-published stories. Deliberately avoided a third 'local AI box' and a second smart-glasses card (RayNeo GT Max) and the IFA home-robot cluster (Ecovacs stain robot, CNET mothership, Acemate tennis robot) so the five spread across five outlets and five device categories.
